name: albanian_02
context: A Facebook comment under a post by the National Institute of Public Health of Kosovo during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. The comment is in Albanian, mostly the informal Kosovo (Gheg) dialect, often written without the letters ë and ç.

versions.analysis_for_next:
Version 0 under-predicts neutral, the majority class at about 57% of gold. 122 neutral texts went to negative and 48 to positive, while gold positive and gold negative were mostly right. So these annotators keep negative and positive for explicit, directed stance and put a great deal in neutral.

The main neutral→negative errors fall into five groups:
- Worry or sadness about rising numbers ('Sa keq, numri kaq i larte', 'Tmerr asht kjo... katastrof').
- Criticism of citizens for not wearing masks.
- Pointed questions or demands to the institute about data, towns or tests ('Pse ka Mitrovica...', 'E per Ferizaj?').
- Musings that cases are under-counted, and conspiracy doubts.
- Banter about towns 'leading the table', jokes about the lab staff ('Koka qu sot heret ai i laboratorit'), and tagging friends with teasing remarks.

The main neutral→positive errors fall into four groups:
- 'Hajde ma gjall' cheering of numbers.
- Condolences.
- Appeals to wear masks or stay home.
- Town pride ('Prishtina kampion') and unrelated congratulations.

Fix: make neutral the explicit default and narrow negative to clear hostility aimed at the institute, government or authorities. That covers calling them liars, insults, curses, open mockery of them, or angry 'enough' complaints at them. Narrow positive to explicit thanks, praise, blessings or relief that the virus is fading, aimed at people or at the outcome. Appeals to citizens, sports-style cheering and condolences become neutral. Keep the sarcasm note. Keep negative cues like rrene, mashtrim and insults to the authorities.

Version 1 overcorrected. Neutral precision rose, but 68 gold-negative texts became neutral, and 18 gold-positive texts did too.

The gold negatives the model missed fall into five groups:
- Bare exclamations of horror or despair: 'tmerr', 'Mjerim', 'Kjamete', 'Boll keq', '15 te vdekur, tmerr', 'Pom tmeroni'.
- Angry scolding of citizens with insults: 'popull budall', 'popell i fliqt', 'Peshë u qu ky popull'.
- Curses and swearing, even aimed at the virus: 'qija nanen'.
- Claims that the numbers are not real or are hidden: 'Ky nuk ashte numer real', 'mos i fshehni', 'shum ka dyshime'.
- Remarks that a town 'lost control' or 'failed', complaints that measures are pointless or wreck the economy, and fed-up 'u lodhum' (we're worn out).

So for these annotators negative is a strong negative emotion of any target, not only hostility toward the authorities.

The gold positives the model missed include:
- Hopeful or encouraging appeals: 'Do e kalojm edhe këtë sfid' (we'll get through this challenge too), 'Shendet per te gjithë' (health to all).
- 'bravo' combined with cheering.
- Good-news remarks: 'lajm mat mir', 'mir asht sonte', 'nice'.

The neutral wins of version 1 must stay: calm questions, requests for data, speculation and calculations, joking banter about towns or staff, bare orders like 'Mshelni kafet' (close the cafés), and mild worry.

New boundary:
- Negative means strong negative emotion: horror or despair words, insults or curses at anyone, accusations of fake or hidden numbers, anger at the measures, and towns 'failing' or losing control.
- Neutral means calm or playful, with no strong emotion word.
- Positive means praise, good news, hope, or an encouraging appeal.

Version 3 was 415 words, so I trimmed it below 400 and kept the same boundaries. I shortened the rule, dropped one positive and one neutral example, and cut a few cues.

The content changes from version 2 stay:
- Mockery or blame aimed at the institute or admin is negative, even as a joke (inflated numbers, errors, the admin being drunk, acting too late).
- Reasoned critiques of citizens, arguments that testing misses cases, and calculations are neutral.
- Town pride, off-topic congratulations, sports talk and predictions are neutral.

Version 3 made mockery of the admin or institute negative. That pushed 65 gold neutrals into negative, which cost more than the 28 negatives it recovered, so macro-F1 dropped slightly to 79.6.

Many gold-neutral texts are playful jokes about the lab, admin, hackers or delays:
- 'Koka qu sot heret ai i laboratorit' (the lab guy got up early today)
- 'Admini ne deti' (the admin's at the seaside)
- 'Hackerat' (hackers)
- 'Ja kan marr doren aparatit' (they've got the hang of the machine)
Many others are reasoned critiques, speculation, quarantine calls and COVID denial. The annotators are inconsistent here, so the best strategy is the version 2 balance (79.7) with narrow refinements.

The refinements are:
- Negative comes back to strong emotion: horror or despair, fed-up expressions ('Na lodhet' (you've worn us out), 'u lodhum' (we're worn out), 'Boll keq' (bad enough)), insults and curses, explicit claims that the numbers are fake or hidden, and anger at measures or government.
- Playful jokes about the admin or lab stay neutral unless they insult or clearly say the numbers are invented.
- Positive gains relief cues: 'Shyqyr' (thank God), 'Ska mo virus' (there's no more virus), 'Perhajr' (congratulations/blessings), 'mir asht sonte' (it's good tonight).
- Town pride, off-topic congratulations and calculations stay neutral, even when they mention recoveries.

The same content as version 5, trimmed below 400 words. I dropped one neutral example and shortened some cue lists and descriptions.

The changes from version 4 remain:
- Cues for lying accusations: 'rreni' (you're lying), 'prralla' (fairy tales), 'dyshime' (suspicions).
- A narrow example of the 'admin, stop your hand' joke, which says the numbers are inflated and is negative.

This is the same content as version 6, trimmed below 400 words. I shortened the rule and the neutral description and dropped a few cues.

The changes from version 5 remain:
- Doubting the virus or its danger is neutral unless it says the institute lies.
- Mild worry words ('sa keq' (how bad), 'alarm', 'kuku' (oh dear)) are neutral.

Version 6 fell to 80.4 from version 5's 82.3, and its edits did not help:
- The virus-doubt example and the mild-worry cues barely reduced neutral→negative errors (58 to 55).
- Dropping 'e hupi kontrollen' (lost control) lost several gold negatives.
- Dropping 'ngushllime' (condolences) turned a condolence into positive.
- Labelling 'sa keq' (how bad) neutral flipped 'Lenna Shabani sa keq'.

The remaining errors are largely annotator inconsistency. 'Tmerr asht kjo... katastrof' is gold neutral, yet '15 te vdekur, tmerr' is gold negative. Admin jokes are labelled both ways.

I will go back to version 5, the best so far, with its wording and cues intact. I will keep only one harmless refinement inside the word limit: condolences named in the positive not_for. Further broad shifts in either direction have each cost more than they gained.

Version 7, nearly identical to version 5, scored 81.2 against 82.3, so roughly a point is run-to-run noise.

The largest error cell is still neutral→negative (62). Most of these texts carry no strong emotion word, insult or lying accusation. They are:
- Remarks about rising numbers.
- Criticism of citizens or families.
- Long proposals for measures.
- Pointed questions to the institute.
- COVID doubts.
- Jokes about a town or the admin.
The model infers negativity from the topic alone.

The gold negatives it misses mostly do contain an explicit marker: a curse, an insult ('bosa' (empty-headed)), a lying accusation, 'deshtu' (failed), 'e hupi kontrollen' (lost control), 'tmerr' (horror), or blame of the government.

So I will add a tie-break: negative needs an explicit marker of that kind. A bad topic, a complaint phrased as a question, a proposal, or scolding of citizens without insult is not enough, and in doubt the answer is neutral. I will also add 'deshtu' (failed) and 'nuk osht real' (not real) to the negative cues.

Version 8 is the best so far at 83.1. The tie-break toward neutral cut neutral→negative errors to 27 and lost only a few negatives.

Some negatives were missed only because their explicit markers had dropped out of the cue list:
- 'shum ka dyshime' (lots of suspicions): the 'dyshime' cue was lost in version 8.
- 'shum bosa jeni' (you're so empty-headed): an insult with no cue.
- 'na muret n qaf' / 'na murren nqaf' (you're killing us): no cue.

I will add these back as cues, which matches the explicit-marker logic. To stay under 400 words I will tighten some wording elsewhere. The rest of version 8 stays unchanged, because further boundary shifts have mostly traded errors one for one.

Version 9 is the best so far at 84.0. The remaining errors are mostly annotator inconsistency: neutral texts with 'tmerr' (horror), jokes about the admin labelled both ways, and positive texts with sarcastic-looking wording.

One clear fix remains. 'Ide palidhje karantina...' (pointless idea, the quarantine) is a missed negative, and its marker 'palidhje' (pointless) dropped out of the cue list in version 8. I will restore it.

To stay under 400 words, I will remove the redundant 'Condolences' from the positive not_for, since 'ngushllime' (condolences) is already a neutral cue, and drop 'numbers' from the neutral cues. Everything else stays as in version 9, to keep its balance.
